evals.name: next-target-directory-runtime-contract
evals.prompt: Scaffold next-cloudflare into ./apps/portal while the current shell remains at the monorepo root.
evals.expected_output: Every post-create command targets ./apps/portal explicitly, the project declares @google/design.md, and the generated project exposes an offline project-local design audit.
expectations: Every dependency command uses pnpm --dir with the explicit project directory instead of relying on prior cd state.
The development dependencies include @google/design.md alongside the existing Next.js scaffold tooling.
The generated scripts expose design:audit as designmd lint DESIGN.md.
Generated instructions use pnpm design:audit and contain no npx, pnpm dlx, bunx, uvx, or runtime package resolution instruction.

evals.name: astro-target-directory-runtime-contract
evals.prompt: Scaffold astro-cloudflare into ./sites/docs while the current shell remains at the workspace root.
evals.expected_output: Astro setup removes the minimal generator's empty astro.config.mjs before the controlled overlay, preserves but does not rewrite its README, and keeps dependency installation plus helper paths scoped to ./sites/docs. The generated design audit uses the declared project-local designmd dependency and never resolves that analyzer at audit time.
expectations: Astro integration and dependency commands use pnpm --dir with the explicit project directory; the known generator astro.config.mjs conflict is removed before overlay publication.
The development dependencies include @google/design.md alongside the existing Astro scaffold tooling.
Generated helper-file and CSS paths are explicitly rooted under the project directory.
The generated project exposes pnpm design:audit and contains no npx, pnpm dlx, bunx, uvx, or runtime package resolution instruction.

evals.name: generated-cross-agent-design-handoff
evals.prompt: Inspect both generated scaffold templates and verify how a user installs the shared Design System skill and audits DESIGN.md afterward.
evals.expected_output: Routes to references/setup-next-cloudflare.md and references/setup-astro-cloudflare.md, verifies the canonical AGENTS.md plus thin Claude adapter, confirms that both templates use the installed skills CLI for the optional shared skill and the declared project-local designmd dependency, and stops rather than falling back to runtime package resolution when that dependency is unavailable.
expectations: Both generated projects use AGENTS.md as the canonical instructions, keep CLAUDE.md as the exact @AGENTS.md adapter, and place shared rules under .agents/rules.
Both generated templates document skills add coroboros/agent-skills --skill design-system without npx.
Both generated package script sets expose design:audit as designmd lint DESIGN.md.
The setup references and generated templates contain no npx, pnpm dlx, bunx, uvx, or @latest runtime resolution path for Design System.

evals.name: occupied-target-hard-stop
evals.prompt: Scaffold next-cloudflare into an existing project that already has package.json.
evals.expected_output: The preflight reports target=occupied and exits nonzero. The skill stops without asking to overlay, migrate, or overwrite the existing project.
expectations: The workflow treats target=occupied as a hard stop rather than a confirmation prompt.
No framework CLI, dependency install, template overlay, or file write runs after the occupied-target result.

evals.name: safe-name-path-and-generator-contracts
evals.prompt: Scaffold next-cloudflare into `./customer portals/customer-portal`, then explain the equivalent Astro generator contract. Reject unsafe package and target names before running either generator.
evals.expected_output: Quotes every project directory and project name interpolation, preserves a parent path containing spaces, rejects invalid final target names plus `node_modules` and `favicon.ico` before environment checks, and uses deterministic non-interactive generator flags. Next.js stays on create-next-app 16 with --no-linter, --no-react-compiler, --use-pnpm, --disable-git, --no-agents-md, and --yes. Astro uses create-astro 5 only as the compatible generator, then explicitly installs the Astro 6 runtime stack into the quoted target.
expectations: A valid target under a parent path containing spaces is passed as one argument through preflight, generation, overlay, dependency installation, and verification; an invalid final target directory name fails before generation.
Reserved npm names node_modules and favicon.ico fail before pnpm, node, or target-state checks.
The Next.js generator suppresses its own instructions, React Compiler, linter, and git initialization with documented flags and runs without prompts.
The Astro generator/runtime major split is explicit: create-astro 5 scaffolds, then astro 6 and its compatible Cloudflare adapter are installed.

evals.name: prerequisites-fail-before-generation-or-overlay
evals.prompt: Scaffold astro-cloudflare when Node 22.11.0 is active and jq is unavailable. Explain how the strict TypeScript config is applied after prerequisites are repaired.
evals.expected_output: Preflight requires stable even-numbered Node >=22.12.0, pnpm, and jq and exits nonzero before generation when any prerequisite is missing. Odd-numbered Node releases report node=unsupported. The overlay requires and validates jq and both JSON inputs before writing templates. create-astro 5 is invoked without the unsupported --typescript flag; the shared overlay installs the strict Astro tsconfig deterministically.
expectations: Node 22.11.0 is reported as too old with required=22.12.0; prerelease and odd-numbered versions report node=unsupported.
A missing jq result blocks before the framework generator; overlay validation also occurs before any template or package.json write.
The Astro generator command has no --typescript flag, and the overlay writes a tsconfig extending astro/tsconfigs/strict.
The generated project records Node 22.12.0 in .node-version and provides .dev.vars.example without overwriting user secrets.

evals.name: generated-ui-baseline-contracts
evals.prompt: Inspect the generated Tailwind, shadcn/ui, and package-name contracts for both scaffolds, including a scoped npm project name.
evals.expected_output: Both scaffolds retain a working Tailwind v4 import. Astro generates a page that imports its global stylesheet and never references tailwind.config. Next initializes the declared shadcn 4 project dependency through pnpm exec without an ephemeral package runner. The validated npm package name, including a scoped name, is written to package.json while the derived Cloudflare slug remains machine-safe.
expectations: The shared overlay ensures exactly one @import "tailwindcss" statement while preserving existing CSS content.
The generated Astro page imports src/styles/global.css, and generated Astro instructions use Tailwind v4 CSS-first tokens without tailwind.config.
Next declares shadcn@4 and runs the project-local CLI through pnpm exec with explicit non-interactive defaults; it uses no npx or pnpm dlx path.
package.json receives the validated npm name verbatim, while Wrangler templates continue to use the derived Cloudflare-safe slug.
